stories.headline: Kerry James Marshall Retrospective Highlights Black Representation in Western Art
stories.dek: A major travelling exhibition brings the celebrated African-American creator's landmark works to broader audiences.
stories.body:
The profound impact of Kerry James Marshall on contemporary visual arts is receiving fresh acclaim through a new travelling retrospective. Recognized widely for shifting the paradigm of institutional fine art, Marshall has spent decades securing a permanent space for Black figures within the traditionally exclusive walls of Western galleries.

According to coverage from Africanews, the artist's contributions are considered by many critics to surpass those of any other living contemporary in terms of expanding racial visibility across mainstream gallery spaces. His canvases challenge historical omissions, offering monumental portrayals of Black everyday life, history, and culture.

The touring exhibition provides a rare opportunity for global audiences to witness the scale and intricacy of his creations firsthand. By placing Black subjects at the absolute center of high art narratives, Marshall continues to influence how cultural institutions curate and perceive historical and modern representation.

Art enthusiasts and critics alike are tracking the retrospective's journey as it moves through various cultural hubs, serving as both a celebration of a legendary career and a vital educational platform for the next generation of creative minds.

stories.headline: CyberAlliance President Larry Yon II Urges African Tech Sector to Aim for Global Scale

stories.body:
Africa’s technology ecosystem possesses the raw ingredients necessary to construct world-class infrastructure, but unlocking that potential requires strategic shifts in capital and vision. This perspective forms the core of a recent conversation between CyberAlliance president Larry Yon II and Phathisani Moyo for TechCabal’s Coffee With… series.

Tracing his entrepreneurial path from an initial, unsuccessful business venture in South Africa to co-founding an artificial intelligence cybersecurity powerhouse, Yon reflects on the hard-learned lessons of building technology enterprises on the continent. His journey underscores the resilience required to navigate early-stage failures and transform them into scalable international operations.

A central theme of the discussion focuses on digital trust and the vital role played by diaspora investment. By leveraging financial resources and expertise from international networks back toward local ecosystems, the continent can better position itself to create foundational infrastructure akin to global giants like NVIDIA.

The interview offers deep insights into the hurdles and triumphs defining modern African tech. As leaders like Yon continue to champion robust cybersecurity frameworks and cross-border collaboration, the roadmap toward a self-sustaining digital economy becomes increasingly clear.
